record.prompt: Please run scripts/cost.sh on data/orders-2026-10.tsv and tell me the total shipping cost for October. Don't edit the script or data/zone-rates.tsv.

base_changes.keywords: cost.sh zone-rates CRLF no rate for zone
base_changes.content: scripts/cost.sh fails with 'no rate for zone "north"' because data/zone-rates.tsv has CRLF line endings (zone keys end in \r). Workaround without editing files: pass a CR-stripped copy as the 2nd arg: tr -d '\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv > /tmp/rates.tsv; sh scripts/cost.sh ORDERS /tmp/rates.tsv

memory_calls.input: memcue add -kind pitfall -source tool -keywords "cost.sh zone-rates CRLF no rate for zone" -- "scripts/cost.sh fails with 'no rate for zone \"north\"' because data/zone-rates.tsv has CRLF line endings (zone keys end in \r). Workaround without editing files: pass a CR-stripped copy as the 2nd arg: tr -d '\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv > /tmp/rates.tsv; sh scripts/cost.sh ORDERS /tmp/rates.tsv"

record.final_answer:
The total shipping cost for October is **58.01**, across 6 orders.

| Order | Zone | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A-1001 | north | 6.94 |
| A-1002 | south | 6.28 |
| A-1003 | island | 15.25 |
| A-1004 | north | 15.10 |
| A-1005 | south | 9.03 |
| A-1006 | north | 5.41 |

The script failed the first time with `no rate for zone "north"`. That's because `data/zone-rates.tsv` uses Windows (CRLF) line endings, so the script read the zone names with a hidden carriage-return character at the end, and they didn't match the zones in the orders file. The orders file doesn't have this problem.

I didn't change the script or the rates file. Instead, I made a cleaned-up copy of the rates file in a temporary directory and passed it to the script as its optional second argument. The repo is unchanged. I also checked the first line by hand: 4.90 + 0.85 × 2.4 = 6.94.

To fix this for good, convert `zone-rates.tsv` to Unix line endings, or make the script strip `\r`. I didn't do either since you asked me not to edit those files.

I saved this problem and the workaround to the session memory as a pitfall so later sessions don't hit it again.
